positions.commentary: Meta was lucky to survive the shift from desktop to mobile and actually had a better business at the other end.
It is unclear if Google will be a better business in five or ten years.

thesis: This episode argues that while AI presents potential benefits for Google like improved ad performance, it remains an open question whether AI constitutes a new platform or merely an enabler. The speaker suggests that Google's search product must endure changes to stay relevant, but it is unclear if these shifts will leave the company with a worse business or if it will be a better business in five or ten years. Consequently, a conservative investor should not make Herculean assumptions about Google's ability to navigate these competitive changes.

claims.claim: Meta was lucky to survive the shift from desktop to mobile and actually had a better business at the other end.
claims.quote: Meta, in some sense, was lucky that they not only survived the platform shift from desktop to mobile, but actually had a better business at the other end.

claims.claim: AI could be great for Google by improving ad click-through rates and creating compelling ads, but it is an open question if AI is a new platform or just an enabler.
claims.quote: Or, it could just be a feature enhancer for devices and products, which could be great for Google, as they lean on AI to improve advertising click-through rates, and generative AI to create more compelling ads.

claims.claim: Google's search product will have to endure changes to stay relevant, and it is unclear if they will leave Google a worse business.
claims.quote: And on that note, it is becoming increasingly clear that Google's search product will have to endure changes to stay relevant in the future. The exact changes Google will need to make are unknown and speculative, and whether they leave Google a worse business is also unclear.

claims.claim: A conservative investor would want to get a reasonable return without making Herculean assumptions on Google's ability to navigate competitive changes.
claims.quote: A conservative investor would want to be able to get a reasonable return without making Herculean assumptions on Google's ability to navigate the changes in competitive dynamics.

claims.claim: It is unclear if Google will be a better business in five or ten years.
claims.quote: Is Google going to be a better business in five years from now? How about 10?
